correctness.limitations: Geometric components and generic structure are taken over an algebraic closure. The result describes augmented endomorphisms, not the unrestricted scheme on nonreduced test algebras. The claim that point counts miss the nonreduced component refers to its nilpotent structure, not its reduced support. Small-field enumeration corroborates only those cases; neither a full local structure theorem for the thickening nor formal verification is claimed.
correctness.rationale: Over each commutative test algebra, the images of x and y for an augmented homomorphism independently lie in the augmentation ideal and must have p-th power zero. This gives the product as schemes. Characteristic p Frobenius kills each nonconstant monomial's p-th power over the universal coefficient algebra, so there are no equations in that characteristic. Otherwise the mixed degree-p coefficients of u=ax+by+w force ab=0 on field-valued points. When a≠0, writing u=xH+W(y), the coefficient of x^(p−1) is W times a unit, whose constant term is p a^(p−1); this forces W=0. The symmetric argument works for b, and with a=b=0 the total degree bound gives u^p=0. These tests over the algebraic closure establish the union with reduced structure. They also show scheme-theoretically on the principal open a≠0, over any test algebra, that the equations are equivalent to W=0; similarly on b≠0. For p=2 outside characteristic two the only equation is 2ab=0, so the scheme is reduced and the third subspace lies in the intersection. For p≥3 the three linear spaces are distinct irreducible components. More precisely than a generic tangent comparison, the coefficient ideal is contained in (a,b)^2 because both w^p and p w^(p−1)(ax+by) vanish by total degree at least 2p−1. At the prime (a,b) of the third component the quotient is zero-dimensional and has a nonzero maximal ideal, since its cotangent space has dimension two there. This proves generic nonreducedness. Monomial counts give axis dimensions p(p−1), third dimension p²−3 and axis–third intersection dimensions p(p−1)−1; the axis–axis intersection cancels the triple intersection in inclusion–exclusion. Counts over extensions therefore give the rational zeta function, and the endomorphism count is the square. Independent direct small-field checks give 8,15,128,6561 for N_p at (p,q)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3), respectively.

value.rationale: This gives characteristic-sensitive geometry for a natural family of local complete intersections and distinguishes two generically smooth components from a thickened one even though a point census records only the reduced spaces. The arithmetic formulas are uniform consequences of that classification rather than isolated computations. This geometric distinction is useful independently of the previously covered p=3 arithmetic.
